title: PRD: Graded Eval Escalation and Safe-Degrade Schedule for Optimize
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Purpose: Define a graded escalation ladder and an automated safe-degrade schedule for Optimize evaluation signals to reduce blast radius from regressions while preserving signal fidelity. Background: We have intermittent regressions detected by Optimize evals that are noisy at low sample sizes and sensitive to promptset drift. Current approaches (binary aborts or full rollbacks) are too coarse and force manual triage. This PRD specifies a multi-stage activation model (inform, restrict, degrade, rollback) tied to composite regression signals and traffic exposure budgets. Scope: - In-scope: promptset stratification rules; composite regression scoring (accuracy, hallucination, latency, safety); staged traffic shaping controls (percent limits, throttles); automated schedule for progressive degradation and rollback; dashboard and alerting templates; runbook skeleton. - Out-of-scope: model re-training workflows; per-customer private deployment specific controls (handled by Dedicated/Private teams separately). Goals: 1) Reduce customer-visible regressions by 60% for eval-detected issues without increasing false aborts by more than 10%. 2) Ensure most incidents can be remediated automatically to a safe degraded state within 15 minutes of detection. 3) Provide clear actionability and signal explainability so on-call and PMs can make informed manual decisions when needed.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Promptset stratification defined and implemented for three axes: intent-cohort, length quantile, and safety-susceptibility tag; each promptset contains >=5k examples for primary production cohorts or a weighted sample plan for low-volume cohorts.

2) Composite regression score implemented as weighted aggregator: delta_accuracy, delta_helpfulness, hallucination-rate delta, and per-response latency delta. Weighting matrix documented and editable in Console.

3) Graded escalation ladder implemented with 4 states: Notice (informational), Restrict (traffic cap 20%), Degrade (traffic cap 5% + simplified template responses for high-risk cohorts), Rollback (full traffic revert to previous model). Transitions are automated based on sustained composite score breach windows (see thresholds).
4) Canary exposure limits configurable per-deployment with defaults: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% revert path, and AB-run increments capped at 2x per 24h unless manually approved.

5) Alerts and dashboard: per-promptset composite score, cohort-level trends, and traffic shaping status appear in Console board; alert on Notice->Restrict and Restrict->Degrade transitions with runbook links.

6) Automated safe-degrade executed within 5 minutes of breach confirmation for Restrict->Degrade paths and within 15 minutes for Degrade->Rollback when escalation criteria met and auto-rollback enabled.
7) Regression false-positive rate measured in a sampling QA bucket does not exceed 10% over a 7-day rolling window after launch.
8) Documentation and runbook published with example triage flows, owner contacts, and manual override steps.
9) Performance measurement: end-to-end action (signal detection to degrade) logged and median time < 8 minutes in staging prior to release.
10) Feature flags present to disable auto-rollback per workspace and to set emergency-stop for platform-wide incidents.
decision_log: 2026-02-12 - Decided to use a composite regression score vs single-metric thresholds to reduce volatility; weighted approach chosen to balance safety and utility. Owners: PM + Applied ML.
2026-02-18 - Chose 4-stage ladder (Notice/Restrict/Degrade/Rollback) after reviewing incident postmortems that showed binary rollback often caused excessive churn.
2026-02-24 - Traffic cap defaults agreed: Restrict=20%, Degrade=5%; these are conservative and will be tunable per-customer.
2026-03-02 - Agreed to require sustained breach windows (e.g., 30m for Notice->Restrict; 2h for Restrict->Degrade) to reduce flapping; window lengths are configurable.
2026-03-08 - Opted for a sampling QA bucket to measure false positives before any auto action is taken in production for the first 14 days after rollout.
implementation_notes: Owners: PM (Asha Mehta), EM (Jonah Ruiz), Applied ML lead (Priya Anand), Observability lead (Marcus Lee), SRE contact (Elliot Barnes).
Infra: new CompositeSignal service to calculate rolling deltas and evaluate rules; requires event stream from Optimize evals and promptset tagging metadata.
DB: small config store for per-workspace escalation thresholds and traffic caps behind feature flags.
Console: new panel for cohort-level composite scores, a traffic-shaping timeline, and policy editor for ladder thresholds.
Observability: histograms for time-to-action, false-positive counters, cohort-level regressions; integrate with existing SLO dashboards and paging rules.
Safety: include a human-in-the-loop approval gate for auto-rollback on customers with 'no-auto-rollback' policy set.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): implement CompositeSignal service and run against historic eval traces for 2 weeks to calibrate weights and windows.
Phase 1 (internal canary): enable for internal Shadow traffic only + QA bucket for 7 days; verify false-positive rate and time-to-action.
Phase 2 (opt-in customers): enable auto Notice and Restrict for pilot customers (5 customers) with manual approval required for Degrade/Rollback for 14 days.
Phase 3 (gradual): allow auto-Degrade for pilot customers and expand to 25% of eligible workspaces after meeting false-positive criteria; monitor closely for 14 days.
Phase 4 (platform default): enable for all non-enterprise workspaces with opt-out; enterprise customers given an onboarding checklist for tailored thresholds.
rollback_triggers: Primary trigger: composite regression score exceeds critical threshold for Degrade->Rollback window (default: sustained breach for 60 minutes across >3 promptset cohorts).
Secondary trigger: safety-signal spike (classifier-based) where hallucination-rate delta > 3x baseline in 15 minutes for high-risk cohorts.
Manual trigger: on-call or PM can initiate immediate rollback via Console emergency-stop; action is logged and requires post-action review.
Circuit-breaker: if automated rollback occurs more than 2x for the same model/version in 72 hours, suspend auto-rollback and create high-priority incident for platform team.
